quick: Nasal: 2 sprays each nostril once daily (27.5 mcg/spray)
Use lowest effective dose if needed
Use with caution in severe impairment
Nasal mucosa, growth in children, ocular effects
summary: Fluticasone furoate is a potent synthetic corticosteroid. The intranasal spray (27.5 mcg/spray) treats allergic rhinitis symptoms, dosed 2 sprays per nostril once daily in adults. As an inhaled powder it is used for maintenance asthma and COPD (often with vilanterol). It has low systemic bioavailability and a strong topical anti-inflammatory effect; key cautions are nasal local effects and rare systemic corticosteroid effects.
indications: Symptoms of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis (intranasal)
Nonallergic rhinitis symptoms in some formulations
Maintenance treatment of asthma in adults and adolescents (inhaled, often combined with vilanterol)
Maintenance treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (inhaled combination)

dosage.c: Allergic rhinitis, adults and children >=12 yr (intranasal)
dosage.d: 2 sprays (27.5 mcg each) per nostril = 110 mcg/day
dosage.n: Reduce to 1 spray per nostril once daily for maintenance
May increase to 2 sprays per nostril if needed, then step down
Per combination product; not for acute relief

admin: Prime the nasal spray before first use and after periods of non-use as directed
Blow the nose, then spray into each nostril aiming slightly away from the septum; breathe in gently
Use once daily at the same time; for rhinitis, full benefit may take several days
Inhaled powder: exhale away from the device, inhale steadily and deeply, then rinse mouth
Do not use the inhaled product for acute bronchospasm/rescue
moa: Fluticasone furoate is a high-affinity glucocorticoid receptor agonist with potent anti-inflammatory activity. It modulates transcription of multiple inflammatory genes, decreasing production of cytokines, leukotrienes and prostaglandins and reducing infiltration and activation of inflammatory cells (mast cells, eosinophils, neutrophils, lymphocytes) in nasal or airway mucosa. Its furoate ester provides strong topical potency with low systemic exposure.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to fluticasone furoate or excipients
Primary treatment of status asthmaticus or acute bronchospasm (inhaled form)
relative: Recent nasal surgery, trauma or ulcers (intranasal)
Active or quiescent tuberculosis, untreated systemic fungal/bacterial/viral infections, ocular herpes simplex

preg: Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies risk; use the lowest effective dose. Systemic absorption from intranasal/inhaled use is low, but corticosteroids can affect fetal development at high systemic exposure.
lact: It is not known whether intranasal fluticasone furoate is excreted in human milk; systemic levels are low and use is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding. Use the lowest effective dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: Fluticasone furoate is cleared mainly by hepatic metabolism; use with caution in severe hepatic impairment and monitor for systemic corticosteroid effects.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, ketoconazole, cobicistat) - increase fluticasone furoate exposure and risk of systemic corticosteroid effects including Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression; avoid or monitor
moderate: Other systemic or inhaled corticosteroids - additive systemic corticosteroid effects
Long-acting beta-agonists (in combination products) - monitor for cardiovascular and metabolic effects
minor: Live vaccines - reduced immune response if systemically immunosuppressed
interactions.diagnostics: May cause measurable cortisol suppression at high systemic exposure.

serious: Adrenal suppression (HPA axis) with high or prolonged dosing
emergency: Acute adrenal crisis during stress in patients transferring from systemic steroids

monitoring: Nasal mucosa for ulceration, septal changes or candidiasis periodically
Growth velocity in children on long-term therapy
Intraocular pressure / signs of cataract in at-risk patients
Signs of adrenal suppression with high-dose or prolonged use
counsel: Use once daily at the same time; benefit may take a few days to develop fully
Aim the spray away from the nasal septum to reduce nosebleeds
Report frequent nosebleeds, persistent nasal pain, or vision changes
For inhaled product, rinse the mouth after use to prevent oral thrush; do not use for sudden symptoms
Do not stop abruptly if transferred from oral steroids without advice
pk: Symptom relief over hours to days (rhinitis)
Low plasma levels; Tmax ~0.5-1 h when detectable
Store at room temperature; keep upright (nasal spray)
pearls: Once-daily intranasal dosing distinguishes it from twice-daily older intranasal steroids
Furoate ester gives high topical potency with very low oral bioavailability
Inhaled fluticasone furoate (often with vilanterol) is a once-daily maintenance option for asthma/COPD
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir) can raise systemic exposure and cause Cushingoid effects
missed: If a once-daily dose is missed, use it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular once-daily schedule; do not double up.
overdose: Acute overdose is unlikely to cause clinically significant problems given low systemic absorption. Chronic excessive use can cause systemic corticosteroid effects (HPA-axis suppression, Cushingoid features). Continue at the recommended dose and monitor adrenal function if overuse is suspected.
